rationale: This is essentially "Redeployable Collateral Value" with the B/M leg swapped for the capital-structure wedge — a highly correlated valuation substitute — so it is a cosmetic variant of an already-tested winner, and it also silently re-signs the wedge (archived with EXPECTED_SIGN negative) without acknowledging that the original hypothesis was contradicted.

The composition-versus-coverage distinction (act/at vs act/lt) is a genuine diagnostic that separates two economically different readings of the archive's strongest alpha leg, though act/lt is close to the classic Graham net-current-asset/current-ratio family and the value interaction structure is by now well-worn.

The construct is dominated by act/at and will be near-collinear with the archived winner, and the stated unification is not what the expression computes — the predecessor liability result was lct/lt (maturity mix) while this uses lct/at, which conflates maturity structure with leverage level.

Internally consistent and a genuinely different economic claim (maturity gap rather than level), and it is an honest falsification test of the duration reading, though prior archive evidence that both act/at and lct/lt carry positive alpha makes near-total cancellation the likely outcome.

Earnings-minus-operating-cash-flow is the accruals anomaly (Sloan 1996) and interacting accruals with value is well-trodden; changing the deflator from assets to liabilities is a cosmetic re-scaling that does not make this a new mechanism, and pi (pretax) versus oancf (after-tax) makes the gap partly a tax artifact.

Pairing a slope-bearing leg with an alpha-bearing leg on a clear "pay from operations or realize from assets" rationale is defensible and the specific pair is untested, but equal-weight SUMRANK of two previously tested components risks simply averaging their evidence rather than strengthening either.
